topic: Hip fracture and registry data quality
usual_baseline: Registry data are fairly complete but not accurate. Only 56% of hip fracture theatre forms were completed and 21% of those fully accurate. Elbow arthroplasty completeness was 63% (radial head 35%). Only 8–10% of records were error-free in one registry. Revisions go missing more than primaries. Coding errors run 50–69% of cases.
fix_that_works: Education plus a checklist sticker: form completion 56% to 81%, accuracy 21% to 56% [1370]. Trainee-led national record checks: elbow completeness 63% to 83%, accuracy 94% to 98% [1689]. An annual NJR audit cycle with named leads and missing-case statements: compliance 92.64% to 97.9% [1635]. A coding-friendly proforma: coding errors 50% to 5% [1657].
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. 100% hip fracture form accuracy was not achieved [1370]. Radial head completeness stayed at 70% [1689], and the revision versus primary gap persisted [1635].
consultant_advice: Only one audit here is on hip fracture data itself; the rest are joint registry and coding. Check a sample of your own entries against the notes, not just form completion. Coding audits show real money lost, £29,325 in one [1657], which gets management attention.
